story: Saraswati is the goddess of knowledge, music, speech and the arts. She is shown in white, seated on a lotus or a swan, playing the veena and holding the Vedas. In the Rigveda she is also a great river, praised as the best of mothers and goddesses.
belief: Students, musicians and artists pray to her before learning or performing. On Vasant Panchami, children often write their first letters, and books and instruments are placed before her to be blessed.
turns: Saraswati has almost no mistakes in the stories, but she keeps her distance from wealth. A popular saying holds that Lakshmi and Saraswati rarely live in the same house, because knowledge and riches pull in different directions.
facts: Many believe the Rigvedic Saraswati river dried up long ago; some link it to the Ghaggar-Hakra river.
She is worshipped in Japan as Benzaiten.
Her swan is said to separate milk from water, a symbol of wisdom telling truth from falsehood.
lessons: Keep learning; knowledge grows when it is shared.
Speech is power, so choose your words with care.
Art and study can be forms of worship.
more: The prayer 'Ya Kundendu Tushara Hara Dhavala' to her is sung in schools across India.
In Bengal, students place their books before her on Saraswati Puja and leave them there for the day.
